sentences.text: Saltriovenator zanellai is the only known species of a ceratosaurian dinosaur that lived in Italy during the Early Jurassic Sinemurian stage. Although no complete skeleton has been found, researchers believe it was a large, bipedal carnivore similar to Ceratosaurus.
The fossil skeleton was shattered by explosives used in quarrying before it could be recovered.
Saltriovenator is considered the largest known theropod before the Aalenian stage, being 25% longer than the Late Jurassic Ceratosaurus.

The first remains were discovered on August 4, 1996, by amateur paleontologist Angelo Zanella in a marble quarry in Saltrio, Italy. The holotype specimen, MSNM V3664, was found in the Saltrio Formation dating to the early Sinemurian, 199 million years ago.
Saltriovenator zanellai was formally named and described in December 2018 by Dal Sasso, Maganuco, and Cau.
Estimated thighbone lengths indicate a body weight between 1,160 and 1,524 kilograms. The femur would have been between 80 and 87 centimeters long, indicating a body weight of 1160 to 1524 kilograms.

Researchers conservatively estimated the holotype individual of Saltriovenator to be between seven and eight meters in length. Saltriovenator would be the largest theropod that lived before the Aalenian epoch, 25% longer than Upper Jurassic Ceratosaurus.
Saltriovenator was likely the largest predator in its region. If it originated from the nearby landmass, Saltriovenator was likely the largest predator in the region.

Phylogenetic analysis in 2018 identified Saltriovenator as a basal ceratosaur and the sister-taxon of Berberosaurus. A 2018 phylogenetic analysis determined Saltriovenator to be a basal ceratosaurian, being the sister taxon to Berberosaurus. Saltriovenator is classified within the parent group Ceratosauria.

During the Late Hettangian to Early Sinemurian, the region was part of the Southern Alps passive margin of Adria, characterized by alternating shallow platforms and subsiding troughs. Fossil pollen indicates a tropical subhumid climate with forests dominated by Hirmeriellaceae and fern understories. Saltriovenator lived in the western Lombardy basin from the early Jurassic, spanning the Hettangian to early Sinemurian stages. Saltriovenator lived between 199.5 and 192.9 million years ago during the Sinemurian stage.

A significant continental area existed near the fossil site with a previously underestimated size, characterized by a warm and humid paleoclimate. Researchers suggest Saltriovenator originated from a nearby landmass rather than distant emergent zones like the Trento Platform.
